An explicit six-spin Hamiltonian and five positive-exchange pulse segments
implement the exact two-outcome instrument

    rejected effect        = I - P_{J_data=0}.

The accepted operation preserves the full logical qubit in the two-dimensional
four-spin singlet multiplicity. Both J_data=1 and J_data=2 are rejected exactly.
Arbitrary local logical gates generated by exchanges among the three untouched
data spins can run concurrently and factor from every helper outcome. The same
helper pair must remain coherent until the final singlet/triplet readout.

There is no energy-gap limit, cold reservoir, scalar-gain positivity premise,
Markov model, or source-band admission in this finite-spin construction. It uses
calibrated equal exchange couplings, a prepared singlet, and controlled isolation.
Physical Hubbard/orbital qualification and actual device performance remain
separate burdens. The previous energy-transfer construction remains valid capital
in EXCHANGE_ONLY_ERASURE_FILTER.txt; it is superseded as the preferred verifier.

    R = s_1+s_2+s_3,
    J_D = R+s_i.

Two helpers a,b start in a singlet |s_ab>. Choose the four simultaneous exchange
edges

    H_star = J [ R dot s_a + s_i dot s_b ]
           = J [ sum_{r=1}^3 s_r dot s_a + s_i dot s_b ],   J>0.   (1)

The three star edges have the same calibrated strength as the separate i-b edge.
During these queries the helper a-b edge and unwanted data edges are off, apart
from explicitly allowed gates on the three r spins. The contact graph is a
three-leaf star plus a disjoint edge. No ferromagnetic exchange is required.

multiplicity one. U is identity on the R=1/2 multiplicity, which becomes the
logical qubit whenever J_D=0.
